sources.locator: "Rebellion of Túpac Amaru II", revision 1376254812, "Siege of Cusco"

explanation: The rebellion's article opens its "Siege of Cusco" section on the march as a decision taken to hold what had been won: **"Seeking to maintain the advantages gained at Quiquijana, Sangarará, and Lampa, he decided to anticipate the enemy and go on the offensive."** The sentences on either side put the same thing in order. Túpac Amaru returned to Tungasuca on 17 December, "the rebel leader began preparations for the great expedition against Cusco", and the army departed on 20 December. The type is `enabled`, because Sangarará is one of three advantages the sentence names and the article weighs none of them. The source supports only that the victory was part of the position the offensive was launched from.
